title: Gold Surges Past $4,500 After U.S. Treasury Doubles Bond Buybacks in Surprise Move
excerpt: Spot gold jumps 3.6% to a two-and-a-half-month high as the dollar and long-dated yields tumble on the Treasury's liquidity support announcement.
body:
• Spot gold surged 3.6% to $4,487.91 on Wednesday after the U.S. Treasury Department doubled its liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated bonds to at least $4 billion per operation.
  • The move knocked 30-year Treasury yields sharply lower from near 19-year highs and sent the dollar index down 0.8%, providing a double tailwind for gold.
  • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent signaled he may further increase government repurchases, with some analysts comparing the move to the Fed's 2011 Operation Twist.
  • Gold was on track for a third consecutive weekly gain as of Friday, trading above $4,530, but investors remain divided on whether the buyback program represents soft financial repression or routine market maintenance.

Gold exploded higher on Wednesday after the U.S. Treasury Department made a surprise announcement that caught markets off guard: it would double the size of its liquidity support buyback operations for longer-dated bonds, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation.

Spot gold climbed 3.6% to $4,487.91 per ounce, touching $4,499.20 — its highest level since early June. U.S. gold futures settled 2.8% higher at $4,545.30. By Friday, prices were holding above $4,530 and on track for a third consecutive weekly gain.

Why the Treasury Moved

The announcement came against a backdrop of mounting stress in the bond market. Yields on 30-year Treasuries had climbed to their highest level in nearly 20 years on Tuesday, hitting roughly 5.34% as investors demanded more compensation for lending to a government whose debt has just crossed $40 trillion.

The Treasury's response — effectively absorbing more long-dated supply through buybacks of older, less liquid bonds — was designed to ease liquidity conditions without altering the Fed's monetary policy stance. The program, first launched in May 2024 to improve liquidity in the $32 trillion Treasury market, uses newly auctioned proceeds or cash to repurchase outstanding bonds.

"This was totally unexpected. Very bullish for gold due to lower yields on longer-dated Treasuries and as it may help to bring the dollar lower."

— Robert Gottlieb, former head of precious metals at Koch Supply and Trading

The dollar index fell 0.8% on the day, making dollar-priced gold cheaper for holders of other currencies. Yields on 30-year bonds dropped by as much as 10 basis points, dragging European government bond yields lower in sympathy.

Markets Debate What It Means

The Treasury's move drew sharply divided reactions. TD Securities called it a "jolt of life" for metals, noting that gold investment flows could accelerate amid the combination of Treasury liquidity support, a Federal Reserve willing to look past an energy shock, and a growing stagflation narrative.

Deutsche Bank strategist George Saravelos compared the effect to the Fed's 2011-12 Operation Twist, describing the buybacks as "soft-form financial repression" aimed at holding down longer-dated yields. When coupled with encouraging foreign central banks to use a Fed repo facility rather than sell Treasuries outright, the strategy amounts to a coordinated effort to manage the long end of the yield curve, he argued.

Not everyone sees a decisive shift. Sarah Ying, head of FX strategy at CIBC Capital Markets, called it a "mini" version of past dollar-stress episodes — milder than April 2025's Liberation Day selloff.

"It's really Bessent testing the market, and then the market fighting back."

— Sarah Ying, CIBC Capital Markets

The Fed Complication

Minutes from the Federal Reserve's July 28-29 meeting, also released Wednesday, showed that several officials were prepared to raise rates and many said further hikes may be needed if inflation does not return to the 2% target.

Treasury Secretary Bessent signaled he may further increase repurchases. Two Fed officials later expressed caution about how the Treasury's debt management changes could affect the central bank's monetary policy stance.

Traders are pricing in a 63% chance the Fed holds rates steady next month, with a 37% probability of a hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Gold's Broader Context

Despite the rally, gold remains roughly 20% below its January record of $5,595, weighed down by the U.S.-Iran conflict that has fueled energy inflation and reinforced expectations of tighter monetary policy. Central bank gold buying in the first half of 2026 fell to its lowest since 2022, and outflows from gold-backed ETFs totaled 45 tons in the second quarter.

Brian Lan, managing director of GoldSilver Central, noted that the dollar's weakness has supported not just gold but all precious metals. The metal's trajectory, he said, will ultimately be determined by what the Fed decides to do next and how those decisions shape rate expectations.
